title: Get API access
snippet:
API access is available by approval. Request a key through the email field on the [Waterfall website](https://www.waterfall.io/), or book a call to discuss your workflow. A member of our team reviews every access request. We aim to reply within a couple of hours.
## Request an API key
Enter your work email on our homepage to request access.
## Book a call
Talk through your use case, pricing, and integration with our team.
We work with a limited number of customers so we can provide direct support and plan capacity around each team’s needs. Before enabling access, we take time to understand what you are building, the data you need, and your expected volume. Customers get a dedicated channel with our founders for questions and integration help. You can also email [support@waterfall.io](mailto:support@waterfall.io). For a useful first conversation, share your use case, input types, expected request volume, and required outputs. For a technical issue, include the endpoint, error code, and any known job ID. Keep API keys out of your message. Before the call, explore [use cases](/v1/use-cases/overview), [compare APIs](/v1/introduction), or prepare a sample using the [evaluation guide](/v1/evaluate-waterfall).

title: Waterfall API FAQ
snippet:
Waterfall.io is a B2B data API for go-to-market workflows. Use Waterfall to find people at target accounts, enrich contact and company records, match emails to business profiles, find phone numbers, verify email addresses, and check job changes.

Waterfall combines 30+ data vendors through one API. Coverage varies by provider, so a contact or field missing from one source may be available from another. We evaluate providers on coverage, accuracy, freshness, and cost, and add or remove them as their performance changes. Your team maintains one integration and one set of agreed Waterfall rates, without managing separate vendor connections and contracts. Changes to the vendor mix do not change those rates. Your total cost depends on the services and options you use and your request volume.

For audit scope and security documentation, [contact our team](mailto:support@waterfall.io).

How do I get an API key and pricing?
API access is available by approval. Enter your work email on the [Waterfall website](https://www.waterfall.io/) to request a key, or [book a call](https://www.waterfall.io/book-a-call) to discuss your workflow and pricing. A member of our team reviews every access request; we aim to reply within a couple of hours. We work with a limited number of customers so we can provide direct support and plan capacity around each team’s needs. Once you have a key, send it in the `x-api-key` header. Follow [Authentication](/v1/authentication) and the [Quickstart](/v1/quickstart).
###
​
Does my API key enable every capability?
Waterfall API access depends on the features enabled for your key. A valid key can receive a permission error for an unavailable capability, and adding `include_phones: true` requires phone enrichment access. Confirm the capabilities your workflow needs with [the Waterfall team](mailto:support@waterfall.io), and use the [Errors guide](/v1/errors) to interpret the returned code.

Waterfall billing rules differ by endpoint. [Phone Enrichment](/v1/phone-enrichment-launcher) charges only when a number is returned. [Email Verification](/v1/email-verifier) does not charge for results where `output.email.email_status` is `unknown`. For other operations, follow the endpoint’s billing guidance, your agreed rates, and the result’s [usage breakdown](/v1/inline-usage). [Contact our team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) to confirm how missing or partial results are charged in your planned workflow.

title: Pricing | Waterfall.io
snippet:
# Pay for answers, not for lookups
Outcome-based across every endpoint: a credit is deducted when we return a verified result, never once per vendor we queried to find it

We are charged by our vendors on every request we make on your behalf, including the ones that come back empty. You are not. A credit is deducted only when we hand back a verified result, so the risk of a low-coverage file sits with us rather than with your budget.

Per-credit rates depend on the endpoints you use and the volume you commit to. We quote after running a benchmark on a sample of your own records, because a list price set against someone else's file tells you nothing about what your file will cost.

Straight answer
Because a per-record price is not comparable across vendors and we would rather not pretend otherwise. Two providers quoting the same cent-per-email can differ by a factor of three on what fraction of your file they actually resolve, and the cheaper one is usually the more expensive one once you divide by results. The number that matters is your cost per verified result on your records, and the only honest way to produce it is to run both against the same file. We will do that before quoting, and we will show you the working.

How does Waterfall.io pricing work?
Outcome-based, on credits. A credit is deducted only when we return a verified result — a verified email, a matched profile, a mobile number, a confirmed job change. Requests that come back empty are free, and one credit covers the entire waterfall regardless of how many of our 30+ sources we had to query to get the answer. Per-credit rates depend on the endpoints you use and the volume you commit to, and are quoted after a benchmark on a sample of your own records rather than from a list price.

Every company has different needs. Talk to our team (most likely one of the founders) to share your use case and see how Waterfall can help.

title: Enrich your first contact
snippet:
Set up your API key
You need a Waterfall API key with Contact Enrichment enabled. [Contact the team](mailto:support@waterfall.io) for access and pricing. Requests use your account’s configured rates. Store the key in an environment variable in your terminal:
```
export WATERFALL_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
```
Keep the key on your server or in your local environment. See [Authentication](/v1/authentication) for key management.

```
curl --request POST 'https://api.waterfall.io/v1/enrichment/contact' \
--header "x-api-key: $WATERFALL_API_KEY" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
"email": "person@company.com",
"include_phones": false
}'
```
The response gives you a `job_id` and `start_date`. An illustrative response:
```
{
"job_id": "1a836daa-ec37-4c75-8a10-080ee9b28a13",

```
export WATERFALL_JOB_ID="YOUR_RETURNED_JOB_ID"
curl --get 'https://api.waterfall.io/v1/enrichment/contact' \
--header "x-api-key: $WATERFALL_API_KEY" \
--data-urlencode "job_id=$WATERFALL_JOB_ID"
```
Read `status` before using the output:
| Status | What to do |
|---|---|
| `RUNNING` | Wait before checking the same job again. Respect the [rate limit](/v1/rate-limit). |
| `SUCCEEDED` | Inspect `output.person` for available data and `output.usage` for returned cost information. |
|

```
{
"status": "SUCCEEDED",
"output": {
"person": {
"first_name": "Jordan",
"last_name": "Lee",
"title": "Head of Sales",
"company_name": "Example Company"
}
}
}
```
